A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 87 readable pages, including Appendices A–I. Full text and rendered-page comparisons reveal no material gaps; pages 3–87 are visually identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original filter-injection, hidden-state analysis, and denoising-head experiments in Section 4, including measured ablation accuracies in Table 2 and supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experiments and outcomes, including filter-training results in Table 1, head-ablation accuracies in Table 2, and the extensive appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The low-rank TVS filter, geometric metrics, and denoising-head identification, ablation, and amplification procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six classification datasets, country-capitals, people-profession, and opus-100 English–Chinese translation. Instruction, random-label, and seen/unseen-label scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including zero-shot controls, unmodified ICL, and randomly selected head-ablation controls in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain full-vocabulary greedy evaluation, 2,048 filter-training examples, 512 held-out examples, and the same training budgets, model configurations, and shot/layer/rank settings.

E4.justification: The filter-component ablations, label and instruction analyses, head-ablation threshold sensitivity, attention case studies, and failure-case experiments are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Table 2's p-values, variability entries in Tables 2 and 7, and Appendix A.3's sampling of two demonstration sequences per test example are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports 0.88, 0.00, and 0.84 for training both filter components, W_enc alone, and W_dec alone, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged, including covariance flux in Appendix A.3 and the Hausdorff-entropy definition, theorem, and proof in Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain identical claims about task-oriented information removal and denoising heads as an ICL mechanism.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and applicability limits are unchanged, including the clustering-versus-bijection discussion, generative-task qualifications, and four limitations in Section 5.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same checkpoints, quantization, prompts, optimizer settings, and sampling details. The code-link destination is unchanged; the author email update adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to induction-head and task-vector research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 updates Hakaze Cho's affiliations and email, renumbers affiliations, and hyphenates 'Task-Verbalization Subspace' in Figure 1. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author/contact block and code-link placement are rearranged, and Figure 1's label gains a hyphen. Other figures, tables, and the layout of pages 3–87 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes administrative and small presentation edits while preserving the same methods, empirical evidence, theory, interpretations, and limitations throughout the main text and appendices. These edits do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
